subject: physics
title: Kinetic and gravitational potential energy
key_idea: A moving object has **kinetic energy**: half its mass times its speed squared. An object raised above the ground has **gravitational potential energy**: mass times gravitational field strength times height. When an object falls, one store decreases as the other increases.

blocks.text: Anything that moves has energy in its kinetic store. The faster it moves and the greater its mass, the more energy it has.

blocks.label: Kinetic energy
where: Ek is kinetic energy in joules (J).
v is speed in metres per second (m/s).

items: Only the speed is squared, not the mass.
Doubling the mass doubles the kinetic energy.
Doubling the speed makes the kinetic energy four times bigger.

items.text: A cyclist of mass 70 kg at 8 m/s: Ek = ½ × 70 × 8²
Ek = ½ × 70 × 64 = 2240 J, or about 2200 J.

diagram.alt: Calculate the kinetic energy of a moving object.
diagram.question: A runner of mass {m} kg moves at {v} m/s. Calculate the kinetic energy of the runner.

blocks.text: Rearrange the equation. The speed squared is 2 × Ek ÷ m, so take the square root at the end.

items: Ek = ½ × m × v². Square the speed first, then multiply.
Doubling the speed makes the kinetic energy four times bigger.
To find v, work out v² first, then take the square root.

blocks.text: Lifting an object against gravity transfers energy to its gravitational potential store.

blocks.label: Change in gravitational potential energy
where: ΔEp is the change in gravitational potential energy in joules (J).
g is gravitational field strength in newtons per kilogram (N/kg). It is 9.8 N/kg near the Earth's surface; some questions use 10 N/kg.
Δh is the change in vertical height in metres (m).

items: Use the vertical height only, in metres.
Use the value of g given in the question.

items.text: A person of mass 60 kg at a height of 1.5 m, with g = 9.8 N/kg: ΔEp = 60 × 9.8 × 1.5

blocks.text: A stretched spring also stores energy, in its elastic potential store. That is covered in the forces topics.

items: ΔEp = m × g × Δh, with height in metres.
The value of g depends on the planet. Use the one in the question.
Doubling the height doubles the gravitational potential energy.

blocks.text: When an object falls, its gravitational potential store decreases and its kinetic store increases. Change the mass, height and planet to see the numbers.

diagram.alt: Drop an object from a height and see its gravitational potential energy, kinetic energy at the bottom and speed.

outputs.label: Kinetic energy gained at the bottom

items: With no air resistance, all the gravitational potential energy lost becomes kinetic energy.
The mass cancels out: a heavier object falling the same height reaches the same speed.
Set mg × h equal to ½ × m × v² to find the speed.
A falling object transfers energy from its gravitational potential store to its kinetic store.
Energy lost from one store equals energy gained by the other, if no energy is dissipated.
A higher drop gives more energy and a higher speed.

checks.q: Calculate the kinetic energy of a trolley of mass 2.0 kg moving at 3.0 m/s.
Calculate the gravitational potential energy gained by a 20 kg block lifted through 16 m. g = 10 N/kg.
What happens to the kinetic energy of an object when its speed doubles?
checks.a: It increases four times, because kinetic energy depends on speed squared.

mistakes.right: The speed must be squared: Ek = 0.5 × 50 × 7² = 1225 J.

mistakes.wrong: m = 5040 × 0.5 × 12², because I multiply to find the mass.
The stairs are 175 cm high, so ΔEp = 60 × 9.8 × 175.
mistakes.right: Convert the height to metres first. 175 cm = 1.75 m.

worked_example.question:
At the instant a diver hits the water, the kinetic energy of the diver is 5040 J.
The speed of the diver is 12 m/s.

Calculate the mass of the diver.
worked_example.tip: One mark for the substitution, one for the rearrangement and one for the answer.

mistakes.right: Square the speed. KE = ½ × 70 × 8² = 2240 J, which rounds to 2200 J.
Include g. An answer without the value of g (10 N/kg) is not accepted: 72 × 10 × 7.0 = 5040 J.
That is v². Take the square root to get v = 8.1 m/s.

worked_example.question:
Electricity can be generated using a water turbine.
Water gains kinetic energy by falling from the top of a dam.

Calculate the minimum height that 7.0 kg of water must fall to gain 1300 J of kinetic energy.
Take g = 10 N/kg.
worked_example.tip: Answers that round to 19 m are accepted, such as 18.57 m.

exam_phrases: gravitational potential energy = m × g × h
rock has more energy in its gravitational store
rock transfers more energy (to the water)

mistakes.wrong: The rock dropped from higher hits the water harder.
mistakes.right: Say which stores. The rock has more energy in its gravitational store, then more in its kinetic store, and transfers more energy to the water.

mistakes.wrong: The kinetic energy of the trolley is 0.5 × 2.0 × 3.0 = 3 J.
A motor transferring 4.3 kJ transfers 4.3 J.
mistakes.right: Convert kilojoules to joules. 4.3 kJ = 4300 J.

worked_example.question:
A trolley has a mass of 2.0 kg.

Calculate the kinetic energy of the trolley at a speed of 3.0 m/s.
worked_example.tip: A correct final answer of 9 J scores all 3 marks.
